brief: drawGround() is 9.2 ms against 2.3 ms for the rest of the frame and rebuilds ~650×/sim-day in both seasons — 80% from the grass-wear line (`if (R()<dt*2) groundDirty = true` per walker on grass, courtyard.html ~1867) and the sweeper's trod line beside it, 20% the light bucket. The 'cache' is repainted every few frames. Throttle the wear-driven repaint: accumulate wear as now but set the dirty flag at most once per sim-minute (or dirty-rect the trodden cell), so a walker's path still darkens at the same rate to the eye and the layer repaints ~130–180×/day instead of ~650. Keep the R() draw where it is — removing it reshuffles the world.
successLooksLike: `probes/ground-rebuilds.mjs` reports under 200 rebuilds/day in both seasons; `perf.mjs` frame time drops by more than half against an interleaved HEAD control; a noon frame at a bucket boundary is byte-identical to HEAD; `snow-wear.mjs` ratios unchanged within noise.
avoid: Do not change how much wear a step adds or where it is read — only when the layer is told to repaint. Do not move the R() draw or change its threshold. Interleave the perf control; frame time swings ±30%.
